title: Shimon Peres
description: Former prime minister and president of Israel
wiki_lead:
Shimon Peres ( shee-MOHN PERR-ess, -⁠ez; Hebrew: שמעון פרס [ʃiˌmon ˈpeʁes] ; born Szymon Perski, Polish: [ˈʂɨmɔn ˈpɛrskʲi]; 2 August 1923 – 28 September 2016) was an Israeli politician and statesman who served as the prime minister of Israel from 1984 to 1986 and from 1995 to 1996 and as the president of Israel from 2007 to 2014. He was a member of twelve cabinets and represented five political parties in a political career spanning 70 years. Peres was elected to the Knesset in November 1959 and except for three months out of office in early 2006, served as a member of the Knesset continuously until he was elected president in 2007. Serving in the Knesset for 48 years (with the first uninterrupted stretch lasting more than 46 years), Peres is the longest serving member in the Knesset's history. At the time of his retirement from politics in 2014, he was the world's oldest head of state and was considered the last link to Israel's founding generation, as well as the last Prime Minister to make aliyah rather than being born on territory that would become Israel.
From a young age, he was renowned for his oratorical brilliance, and was chosen as a protégé by David Ben-Gurion, Israel's founding father. He began his political career in the late 1940s, holding several diplomatic and military positions during and directly after the 1948 Arab–Israeli War. His first high-level government position was as deputy director general of defense in 1952 which he attained at the age of 28, and director general from 1953 until 1959. In 1956, he took part in the historic negotiations on the Protocol of Sèvres, which was described by British prime minister Anthony Eden as the "highest form of statesmanship". In 1963, he held negotiations with U.S. president John F. Kennedy, which resulted in the sale of Hawk anti-aircraft missiles to Israel, the first sale of U.S. military equipment to Israel. Peres represented Mapai, Rafi, the Alignment, Labor and Kadima in the Knesset, and led Alignment and Labor.
Peres first succeeded Yitzhak Rabin as acting prime minister briefly during 1977, before becoming prime minister from 1984 to 1986. As foreign minister under Prime Minister Rabin, Peres engineered the 1994 Israel–Jordan peace treaty, and won the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize together with Rabin and Yasser Arafat for the Oslo Accords peace talks with the Palestinian leadership. In 1996, he founded the Peres Center for Peace, which has the aim of "promot[ing] lasting peace and advancement in the Middle East by fostering tolerance, economic and technological development, cooperation and well-being." Peres died in 2016 at Sheba Medical Center after suffering a stroke.

Early life
Shimon Peres was born Szymon Perski, on 2 August 1923, in Wiszniew, Poland (now Vishnyeva, Belarus), to Yitzhak (1896–1982) and Sara (1903–1969, née Meltzer) Perski. grok_lead: Shimon Peres (Hebrew: ×©××¢×× ×¤×¨×¡; born Szymon Perski; 2 August 1923 â 28 September 2016) was a Polish-born Israeli statesman who served as the ninth President of Israel from 2007 to 2014, Prime Minister from 1984 to 1986 and from 1995 to 1996, and multiple times as Minister of Foreign Affairs and Minister of Defense. A key figure in the Labor Party, Peres played a pivotal role in Israel's early state-building, particularly in establishing its defense infrastructure, including arms procurement from France and the development of the Dimona nuclear reactor, which formed the basis of Israel's undeclared nuclear deterrent. Later in his career, he shifted toward diplomacy, co-authoring the Oslo Accords with Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat, earning the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict through mutual recognition and interim self-governance arrangements. Born in Wiszniew (now Vishnyeva, Belarus), then part of Poland, to a Jewish family, Peres immigrated to Mandatory Palestine in 1934 at age 11, joining youth movements affiliated with the Haganah defense organization and later studying at Ben Shemen Agricultural School. His early career in the Defense Ministry under David Ben-Gurion involved clandestine efforts to arm the nascent Israeli military amid international embargoes, establishing domestic industries for aircraft, tanks, and missiles, which were critical for Israel's survival in the 1948 War of Independence and subsequent conflicts. These pragmatic, often covert operations underscored a realist approach prioritizing Israel's security through technological and strategic superiority, though they drew criticism for opacity and reliance on questionable alliances, such as nuclear cooperation with France during the 1950s. Peres's political trajectory included near-misses at leadership, losing the Labor premiership to Rabin in 1974, but he orchestrated unity governments and rotation agreements that stabilized coalitions during economic crises and the Lebanon War aftermath. As Prime Minister in 1984, he initiated economic liberalization to combat hyperinflation, withdrawing forces from Lebanon, and fostering covert ties with African and Asian states; his 1995 term, thrust upon him by Rabin's assassination, saw intensified peace negotiations but ended amid rising suicide bombings that undermined public support for concessions. Critics, including from right-wing perspectives, have highlighted Peres's role in expanding West Bank settlements during his defense tenure in the 1970s and the 1996 Qana artillery incident in Lebanon, where civilian casualties occurred under his command, reflecting the tensions between his security imperatives and later dovish image. As President, a largely ceremonial role, he advocated global innovation and reconciliation, founding the Peres Center for Peace and Innovation to promote practical cooperation. Peres's legacy embodies the evolution from existential defense needs to aspirational peace-building, marked by enduring achievements in state resilience alongside unresolved debates over the costs of ambiguity in nuclear policy and the Oslo framework's causal links to subsequent violence.
